R001.fact: If z∈[0,∞] and z<∞, then z.toReal is a nonnegative ordinary real and ofReal(z.toReal)=z; this is the unique nonnegative real representative of z.

grounds.reason: dimH E takes values in the extended nonnegative reals.
E004 instantiated at the n,E of H001 gives dimH E<∞.
D is defined as (dimH E).toReal, using the real-value map on this codomain.
ofReal embeds each nonnegative real unchanged into the extended nonnegative reals.

R001.justification: The extended nonnegative reals consist of the nonnegative real values together with the top element ∞. A value strictly below ∞ lies in the finite part. On that part the real-value map returns the underlying nonnegative real and ofReal is its inverse. Injectivity of the embedding on nonnegative reals proves uniqueness. Applying this to z=dimH E proves F001 without any new hypothesis.

R002.fact: For each finite n, Rn(n) is second countable in its Euclidean metric. The max metric on Rn(n)×ℝ induces the product topology, is second countable, and its Borel sigma algebra equals the product of the factor Borel sigma algebras.

grounds.reason: Rn(n) is the real finite-coordinate Euclidean metric space, including the one-point case n=0.
The ambient product uses the max metric and its Borel measurable structure.
S001 explicitly uses rational-coordinate boxes and the countable rectangle base to establish these ambient conditions.

R002.justification: For n>0, boxes with rational endpoints are a countable family and form a Euclidean base: each point of an open ball lies in such a box whose coordinate widths are sufficiently small that the sum of squared coordinate displacements stays below the squared radius. For n=0 the singleton is a base. The real line has a rational-interval countable base. A max-metric ball is a product of factor balls, so the max topology is the product topology and products of factor base elements give a countable base. Every product-open set is therefore a countable union of measurable base rectangles. Conversely, inverse images of factor Borel sets under the continuous coordinate projections are Borel. These two inclusions give the stated equality of sigma algebras.

R002.fact: ofReal embeds the nonnegative reals into [0,∞] with finite image, preserving and reflecting weak and strict order and preserving addition on nonnegative arguments. Every x∈[0,∞] with x<∞ has a unique nonnegative finite real representative r=x.toReal with x=ofReal r; hence comparisons between x and ofReal a, for a≥0, are exactly the corresponding real comparisons.

grounds.reason: ofReal and [0,∞] are explicitly the usual nonnegative-real embedding and extended order/addition.
D≥0 and dimH E=ofReal D are already available.
F005 at D+1 gives the finite bound used at the start of S006.
S006 explicitly proves dimH Fmax≤ofReal(D+2)<∞ before interpreting toReal and supplies the midpoint contradiction.

R002.justification: The extended nonnegative reals consist of the ordinary nonnegative real numbers together with a greatest element ∞. Their order and addition restrict to ordinary real order and addition on finite elements, giving the embedding and representative statements. From the displayed finite upper bound, dimH Fmax cannot be ∞, so its representative is nonnegative and finite. Under L2, r>D+1. The midpoint then has qstar>D≥0 and qstar+1<r, making the strict embedded comparison valid. Also ofReal(D+1)=ofReal D+1 since both summands are nonnegative. These are routine representation facts at the existing order step, with no additional hypothesis.

R003.fact: For every finite n, Rn(n) is second countable. Its max-metric product with ℝ is second countable, and the Borel sigma algebra of that metric is the product of the two Borel sigma algebras. Rn(n) is realized by finite real tuples, so also has the stated universe-0 realization.

grounds.reason: Rn(n) is finite-dimensional Euclidean space, including the one-point n=0 case, with its Borel structure.
The ambient product is Rn(n)×ℝ with the max metric and Borel structure.
This is the rational-box and rectangle-base justification actually invoked in S001.

R003.justification: For n>0, boxes with rational endpoints form a countable base: each point in an open Euclidean ball lies in a sufficiently small such box contained in the ball, using the finite-coordinate norm bound. For n=0 the singleton is a finite base. Rational intervals give a countable base for ℝ; products of base members are a countable base for the max metric. Rectangles of Borel sets are Borel by continuous coordinate projections, while every metric-open set is a countable union of basic open rectangles. These two inclusions prove equality of the Borel and product sigma algebras. Finite tuples of real numbers require no larger universe.

R003.fact: For q∈[0,∞], the total real-value map q.toReal takes the finite value of q when q<∞ and takes 0 at ∞. For finite q, t=q.toReal satisfies t≥0 and ofReal t=q. The map ofReal preserves and reflects order on nonnegative reals and preserves their sums. Consequently q<ofReal(D+1), with D≥0 real, implies q<∞, 0≤t<D+1 and q=ofReal t; comparisons with ofReal(sstar+1) can then be made as real comparisons whenever sstar+1≥0.

grounds.reason: ofReal is the nonnegative-real embedding into the usual extended nonnegative reals, with usual order and addition.
N001 supplies the finite nonnegative D and dimH E=ofReal D; L1 implies D>0.
sstar is defined using the total real-value map before the contradiction branch.
L3 bounds q=dimH Fmax by the finite value ofReal(D+1); only within this branch does the proof use the inverse property.

R003.justification: The ordered extended nonnegative reals consist of embedded nonnegative reals together with a greatest element ∞. A value below a finite embedded real is finite and therefore has a unique nonnegative real representative, which is its toReal value. Order and addition on finite representatives are the real ones. Thus all stated inverse, comparison and sum identities follow from the embedding; outside the finite case the total convention gives a defined sstar without granting an inverse identity.

R004.fact: For ordinary metric spaces X,Y, d((x,y),(x',y'))=max(d_X(x,x'),d_Y(y,y')) is a metric on X×Y. Ordinary metrics induce extended metrics by viewing each finite nonnegative distance in [0,∞]; any map preserving all ordinary distances also preserves these extended distances.

grounds.reason: Rn(n) has its stated Euclidean metric, including the one-point case n=0.
The real line carries its usual metric.
The ambient product distance is explicitly the maximum of the two coordinate distances.
S002 computes equality of the ordinary distances for every real pair t,u.

R004.justification: Nonnegativity, symmetry and separation for the maximum follow from those of each coordinate metric. Each coordinate distance between a first and third point is bounded by the sum of the two corresponding product distances, so their maximum obeys the triangle inequality. Embedding the resulting finite distances into [0,∞] preserves the metric axioms and the distance equalities computed in S002.

R005.fact: For d=dimH E in the usual extended nonnegative reals, d≥0 and either d=0 or d>0.

grounds.reason: D007 places dimH E in [0,∞].
D008 specifies the usual extended order on this codomain.

R005.justification: Zero is the least element of [0,∞], giving 0≤d. Totality gives d≤0 or 0<d. In the first case antisymmetry with 0≤d gives d=0; in the second d>0. This also covers d=∞ and needs no finiteness hypothesis.

R005.fact: For a=dimH Fmax and b=dimH E+1 in [0,∞], the inequalities b≤a and a≤b imply a=b.

grounds.reason: D008 gives the dimension codomain its usual extended order and addition.
Case elimination supplies b≤a; instantiation of N002 under L1 supplies a≤b.

R005.justification: The usual order on extended nonnegative reals is antisymmetric, including at infinity. Thus two elements each at most the other are equal; no subtraction or finite-valuedness assumption is involved.

R006.fact: For each natural n, on the real vector space Rn(n)×ℝ the function N(x,t)=max(‖x‖,|t|) is a norm; its induced distance is max(dist(x,y),|t-u|). This includes n=0.

grounds.reason: Rn(n) is the standard real Euclidean normed space, including the zero-dimensional space.
The required product metric is explicitly max(dist(x,y),|t-u|).

R006.justification: Nonnegativity and definiteness follow from those of each component norm. Scalar homogeneity follows by factoring |a| out of the maximum. The component triangle inequalities give N(z+w)≤max(‖x‖+‖y‖,|t|+|u|)≤N(z)+N(w). Applying N to a difference gives the stated distance. No positive-dimension hypothesis is used.

R006.fact: For the linear coordinate bijection e constructed in S001, ‖e(z)-e(w)‖≤sqrt(2)N(z-w), and for its inverse N(e⁻¹(v)-e⁻¹(u))≤‖v-u‖. Thus e and its inverse are continuous, so the constructed linear bijection is a continuous real linear equivalence.

grounds.reason: The paragraph explicitly supplies linearity, the coordinate inverse, and N(z)≤‖e(z)‖≤sqrt(2)N(z) for all z.
The target Euclidean distance is the norm of a difference.
The source distance is the maximum of the component distances.

R006.justification: Apply linearity to differences for the first bound. Apply the lower norm bound to e⁻¹(v)-e⁻¹(u), whose image is v-u, for the second. For any ε>0, the distance thresholds ε/sqrt(2) and ε respectively give the continuity inequalities at every point. These are direct consequences of the displayed bounds and require no compactness or limiting argument.

R007.fact: If f:X→Y is a bijective isometry of metric spaces and A⊆X, then H^a(f(A))=H^a(A) for every positive real a under D006, and consequently dimH(f(A))=dimH(A) under D007. In particular this holds for the coordinate permutation moving the first coordinate of Feuc to the last position.

grounds.reason: N006 explicitly supplies an isometric coordinate permutation from the interval-first realization to the interval-last realization.
D005 specifies that permutation and identifies Feuc and the requested interval-last product.
D006 defines Hausdorff measure using countable covers and diameter-power costs.
D007 defines dimension by the infimum of positive exponents with zero Hausdorff measure.

R007.justification: For each positive scale, a bijective isometry and its inverse transport countable covers between the ambient spaces, preserving empty members, all diameters and each cover's cost. Thus the infima of costs agree at every scale, and taking the defining suprema gives equality of H^a. The sets of positive exponents at which these measures vanish are identical, so their infima defining dimension agree, also when this set is empty. The specified coordinate permutation is bijective with inverse permutation; its isometry property is explicitly supplied by N006.

source_steps.text: Work with arbitrary n and E in H001. Apply E004 to this n and this subset E of Rn(n). It gives dimH E<∞, also when n=0. Define D=(dimH E).toReal. An extended nonnegative real below infinity has a unique finite real representative, its toReal, and this representative is nonnegative; thus D≥0 and ofReal D=dimH E. This uses the ordinary order identification of [0,∞) with the finite part of [0,∞], not compactness or a dimension bound for the product.

The real number D from F001 witnesses the finite nonnegative representative required by the exported conclusion. Its private name is existentially closed in the conclusion. Since n and E were arbitrary under the original nonempty compact hypotheses, this proves the full quantified statement. Compactness and nonemptiness are retained in that statement although the finiteness theorem does not require them.

Use H001 to fix the original n and nonempty compact E. Choose D from N001, with D≥0 and dimH E=ofReal D. The space Rn(n) is a metric space of universe 0 with its specified Borel structure. It is second countable: for positive n, rational-coordinate boxes with rational endpoints form a countable base in the finite Euclidean product topology; for n=0 the one-point topology has a finite base. The max product with ℝ has the product topology, whose countable rectangle base makes its Borel structure equal to the product Borel structure. These facts verify the ambient conditions of the product estimates and the critical-exponent theorem.
Fix an arbitrary real q and temporarily assume L1: D<q. By F001, q>0 and dimH E=ofReal D<ofReal q. Both q and q+1 are nonnegative real exponents, with q+1>0.
Apply the first implication of E003 in Rn(n), with set E and exponent q. The strict dimension inequality in F002 gives H^q(E)=0.

Apply E010 with ambient Rn(n), subset E and exponent q. The ambient premises are F001, positivity is F002 and the zero-measure premise is F003. Its conclusion is H^(q+1)(E×I)=0 in the max product metric, which is H^(q+1)(Fmax)=0 by the definition of Fmax.

Since zero is not infinity, F004 implies H^(q+1)(Fmax)≠∞. Apply the third implication of E003 in the max product Rn(n)×ℝ to Fmax at exponent q+1. This gives dimH Fmax≤ofReal(q+1). Discharge L1 and universally close the arbitrary q: for every real q>D, dimH Fmax≤ofReal(q+1).

Taking the exponent D+1 in F005 gives dimH Fmax≤ofReal(D+2)<∞. Define qstar=(D+(dimH Fmax).toReal-1)/2. Temporarily assume L2: ofReal(D+1)<dimH Fmax. By the preceding finiteness and D≥0, the real representative (dimH Fmax).toReal is greater than D+1. Finite algebra then gives D<qstar and qstar+1<(dimH Fmax).toReal. Thus ofReal(qstar+1)<dimH Fmax, whereas F005 at qstar gives the reverse weak inequality. This contradiction discharges L2 and proves dimH Fmax≤ofReal(D+1). For D≥0, ofReal(D+1)=ofReal D+1=dimH E+1 by F001 and nonnegative-real addition. This is the exported conclusion for the arbitrary original n,E, with no surviving local assumption or dependence on the choice of representative. The same calculation includes D=0 and n=0.

Use H001 and choose the real representative D from N001. Temporarily assume L1: dimH E>0, the additional antecedent in the exported conclusion. Since D≥0 and dimH E=ofReal D, this gives D>0. Rn(n) is a second countable universe-0 metric space with its Borel structure: rational-coordinate boxes form a countable base when n>0, and the singleton space has a finite base when n=0. A countable base of rectangles shows that its max product with ℝ has the product Borel structure and is a Borel metric space.
Fix an arbitrary real s and temporarily assume L2: 0<s<D. F001 yields ofReal s<dimH E. Also s+1>0.
Apply the second implication of E003 to X=Rn(n), A=E and exponent s. The strict inequality in F002 proves H^s(E)=∞.
Apply E020 to X=Rn(n), A=E and s. Its premises follow from F001 and F002, and it gives H^s(E)≤H^(s+1)(Fmax). By F003 the left side is infinity, so H^(s+1)(Fmax)=∞ in the extended nonnegative reals.

Apply the fourth implication of E003 in the Borel max product to Fmax at exponent s+1. From F004 obtain ofReal(s+1)≤dimH Fmax. Discharge L2 and universally close s, retaining only L1: for every real s with 0<s<D this lower bound holds.

Define sstar=(D+max(0,(dimH Fmax).toReal-1))/2. Temporarily assume L3: dimH Fmax<ofReal(D+1). Then dimH Fmax is finite, its real representative is nonnegative and strictly less than D+1, and max(0,(dimH Fmax).toReal-1)<D because D>0. The midpoint definition implies 0<sstar<D and (dimH Fmax).toReal<sstar+1. Consequently dimH Fmax<ofReal(sstar+1), contradicting F005 at sstar. Discharging L3 proves ofReal(D+1)≤dimH Fmax. By F001, ofReal(D+1)=dimH E+1. Discharge L1 to prove precisely the conditional lower bound in the exported conclusion, and universally close the original n,E. No assumption of positive ambient dimension or finiteness of dimH Fmax was used outside the contradiction branch; the representative D has been eliminated from the output.
Fix arbitrary n,E as in H001. Temporarily assume L1: dimH E=0, the antecedent of the exported conclusion. Nonemptiness in H001 supplies a point xzero∈E. This choice is valid even for n=0.

Define f:ℝ→Rn(n)×ℝ by f(t)=(xzero,t), and put C=f''I. For any real t,u, the max product distance between f(t) and f(u) is max(dist(xzero,xzero),|t-u|)=|t-u|. Thus f preserves all distances and is an isometry between these metric spaces, hence also for their extended distances. Moreover C⊆Fmax: each point of C has first coordinate xzero∈E by F001 and second coordinate in I.
Apply M007 to the isometry f and set I. It gives dimH C=dimH I. Apply E005 to the usual closed real interval I=[0,1], obtaining dimH I=1; hence dimH C=1.

Apply M006 to C⊆Fmax in the max product, using F002. It gives dimH C≤dimH Fmax; F003 therefore yields 1≤dimH Fmax. Under L1, dimH E+1=0+1=1, so this is exactly dimH E+1≤dimH Fmax. Discharge L1 and universally close the original n,E to obtain the exported conclusion. The conclusion is independent of the chosen point xzero.

To prove the full universal statement, let the parameter n be arbitrary and temporarily assume L1: E⊆Rn(n) is nonempty and compact. This is precisely the antecedent retained in the exported conclusion, not an extra global hypothesis. Instantiate N001 at this n,E and choose its finite real representative D≥0 with dimH E=ofReal D. In particular dimH E≥0. In the linearly ordered extended nonnegative reals, either dimH E=0 or dimH E>0.
Temporarily assume L2: dimH E=0. Apply N004 at the current n,E with L1 and L2 to obtain dimH E+1≤dimH Fmax. Discharge L2, retaining the implication from this zero-dimensional case.
Temporarily assume L3: dimH E>0. Apply N003 at the current n,E with L1 and L3 to obtain dimH E+1≤dimH Fmax. Discharge L3, retaining the implication from this positive-dimensional case.

Eliminate the exhaustive disjunction in F001 using F002 and F003. It gives dimH E+1≤dimH Fmax. Instantiate N002 at this n,E under L1 to get dimH Fmax≤dimH E+1. Antisymmetry yields dimH Fmax=dimH E+1. Discharge L1 into the nonempty compact antecedent and universally close the arbitrary original n,E. This is exactly the exported conclusion, with Fmax interpreted by D003, and uses no unlisted H input or private fact from another producer.

Fix arbitrary n and an arbitrary subset C⊆Rn(n). Define e=YuiJoinEquiv(n) by D004. It is real linear by coordinate addition and scalar multiplication, is bijective, and has inverse given by deleting the first coordinate to recover the Euclidean n-vector and taking that first coordinate as the real component. For every x∈Rn(n) and t∈ℝ, its Euclidean norm is sqrt(‖x‖²+|t|²). The nonnegative maximum of ‖x‖ and |t| is at most this norm, and the norm is at most sqrt(2) times that maximum, by comparing their squares. Thus e is bounded by sqrt(2) times the max product norm, and its inverse is bounded by the Euclidean norm. Applying these bounds to differences proves continuity of e and its inverse. Hence e is a continuous real linear equivalence between the max-norm product Rn(n)×ℝ and Rn(n+1). This also verifies directly the property of the composition specified in D004. At n=0 the empty coordinate sum is zero, and these formulas and inverse remain valid.

Apply E008 with real normed spaces Rn(n)×ℝ and Rn(n+1), equivalence e from F001, and arbitrary subset C×I. It yields dimH(e''(C×I))=dimH(C×I), where the right hand product has the max metric and the left hand ambient space has its Euclidean metric. No regularity property of C is needed.

Define p on Rn(n+1) by p(t,x_0,...,x_(n-1))=(x_0,...,x_(n-1),t). For any two vectors, the sum of the squares of their coordinate differences is unchanged by this finite permutation. Taking nonnegative square roots shows equality of Euclidean distances, so p is an isometry. In particular p''(e''(C×I)) is precisely the coordinate realization of C×I with the interval coordinate last. At n=0 p is the identity and this conclusion still holds.

Apply M007 to p and the Euclidean set e''(C×I), using F003. It gives dimH(p''(e''(C×I)))=dimH(e''(C×I)). Together with F002, this proves the metric-transfer equality for either coordinate order. The subset C was arbitrary, so universally closing C proves the equality for every E⊆Rn(n), without a nonempty or compact restriction. In particular H001 identifies the original current Fmax=E×I and its Euclidean image Feuc=e''Fmax, giving dimH Feuc=dimH Fmax, with the interval-last image carried by p. Universally closing n proves all clauses of the exported conclusion, including n=0. No equality of the two Hausdorff measures is asserted or used.

For arbitrary n and E satisfying H001, instantiate N005 at this nonempty compact E. It gives dimH Fmax=dimH E+1 in the max product metric. Instantiate N006 at the same n,E: the Euclidean image Feuc has dimension dimH Fmax, and the interval-last coordinate realization is isometric to Feuc and has the same dimension. Substituting N005 into this equality gives dimH Feuc=dimH E+1, and hence dimH(E×[0,1])=dimH E+1 in the requested Euclidean (n+1)-space. Definitions D002–D005 identify the exact interval, product, image and coordinate order. Universally closing n,E proves P for every n≥0, including n=0. The original compactness condition is retained, though no estimate in this selected basis route needs it; nonemptiness was used in the zero-dimensional lower bound.

header:
import Mathlib
open Set MeasureTheory
open scoped ENNReal NNReal
noncomputable section

abbrev YuiRn (n : ℕ) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)

def YuiContent {X : Type*} [EMetricSpace X] (a : ℝ) (r : ℝ≥0∞) (A : Set X) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨅ (U : ℕ → Set X) (_ : A ⊆ ⋃ i, U i) (_ : ∀ i, Metric.ediam (U i) ≤ r),
    ∑' i, (Metric.ediam (U i)) ^ a

def YuiJoinEquiv (n : ℕ) : (YuiRn n × ℝ) ≃L[ℝ] YuiRn (n + 1) :=
  (((PiLp.continuousLinearEquiv 2 ℝ (fun _ : Fin n => ℝ)).prodCongr
      (ContinuousLinearEquiv.refl ℝ ℝ)).trans
    (ContinuousLinearEquiv.prodComm ℝ (Fin n → ℝ) ℝ)).trans
    ((Fin.consEquivL ℝ (fun _ : Fin (n + 1) => ℝ)).trans
      (PiLp.continuousLinearEquiv 2 ℝ (fun _ : Fin (n + 1) => ℝ)).symm)

def YuiI : Set ℝ := Set.Icc 0 1

def YuiFmax (n : ℕ) (A : Set (YuiRn n)) : Set (YuiRn n × ℝ) :=
  A ×ˢ YuiI

def YuiFeuc (n : ℕ) (A : Set (YuiRn n)) : Set (YuiRn (n + 1)) :=
  YuiJoinEquiv n '' YuiFmax n A

def YuiLast (n : ℕ) (z : YuiRn (n + 1)) : YuiRn (n + 1) :=
  WithLp.toLp 2 (fun j => z (finRotate (n + 1) j))

def YuiFeucLast (n : ℕ) (A : Set (YuiRn n)) : Set (YuiRn (n + 1)) :=
  YuiLast n '' YuiFeuc n A

premises.statement: Let n be an arbitrary natural number, E⊆Euclidean n-space be nonempty and compact, I=[0,1], Fmax=E×I with the max product metric, and Feuc the coordinate realization of E×I with the Euclidean metric in dimension n+1. These are the original target hypotheses, including n=0.

For every Borel extended metric space X, A⊆X and d≥0: dimH A<d implies H^d(A)=0; d<dimH A implies H^d(A)=∞; H^d(A)≠∞ implies dimH A≤d; and H^d(A)=∞ implies d≤dimH A. Exponents are nonnegative reals embedded in [0,∞] in dimension comparisons.

The conclusion gives dimH(YuiFeucLast n E)=dimH E+1. By T008 its point map is (x,t)↦toLp 2 (Fin.snoc (ofLp x) t), so its image is exactly the Euclidean coordinate realization of E×[0,1] with the interval last. The coordinate bijection identifies both sets in both directions, with no additional hypotheses; n=0 leaves only t. T009 explicitly justifies max-to-Euclidean dimension transfer and the isometric first-to-last permutation. Thus the displayed equality and the original full quantified Euclidean product equality identify the same dimension statements, with the original nonempty compact hypotheses and extended addition.

conclusion.statement:
Here dimension means **Hausdorff dimension**. As approved by the user on
2026-10-23, assume explicitly that \(E\) is nonempty. With the convention
\(\dim_H\varnothing=0\), the printed equality would otherwise fail for
the empty set. This is a disclosed addition to the printed exercise.

Let \(n\geq0\) be an integer, let \(E\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty
compact set, and put \(I=[0,1]\). Identify \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\)
with \(\mathbb R^{n+1}\) and use its Euclidean metric. Prove

\[
\dim_H(E\times[0,1])=\dim_H E+1.
\]

The zero-dimensional ambient space \(\mathbb R^0\) is included. A later
formalization using a different product norm must justify the metric change.

representation: YuiRn n is EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), i.e. PiLp 2 of the Fin n coordinate family; 2 is the norm exponent and Fin n is the coordinate index type, not a smoothness/order parameter. Its canonical metric and Borel instances are used. The ordinary Lean product YuiRn n × ℝ has the max metric, so YuiFmax is the max-metric product. YuiJoinEquiv is the frozen continuous real linear equivalence with interval coordinate first. YuiLast rotates coordinate arguments, giving the interval-last Euclidean realization YuiFeucLast. T008 verifies the coordinate formulas and isometry; T009 proves the actual change of dimension between metrics and coordinate orders. dimH takes values in ENNReal, with ∞ allowed, and uses the Borel Hausdorff critical exponent. Measure.hausdorffMeasure has the unnormalized diameter-power countable-cover meaning; E003 uses NNReal exponents d coerced to ℝ for measure and ENNReal for dimension. ENNReal.ofReal clips negative reals to zero; every representative/exponent used here has explicit nonnegativity or positivity. The finite witness is existential only in N001 and remains local to each consumer. Parameters n,E and the assembled H001 binder universally close the target. Workload: ten small obligations, with independent upper/lower measure chains, their separate real-order limit arguments, a local-point zero case, and independent coordinate transport. Shared consumers are T001 (T003,T005,T007), T008 (T009), and T009 (terminal). Shared public definitions are only spaces/sets/maps, with no added theorem assumptions. The two strict-exponent families are implementation cuts of the existing NL0 arguments, not new mathematical input. No optional background note is a premise. The exact prepared M006/M007 ports are retained because the frozen 2basis foundation boundary requires them; the scoped calls are recorded in T006 and T009.

namespace YuiBasis
set_option autoImplicit false
set_option Elab.async false in
theorem B003 : ∀ {X : Type*} [EMetricSpace X] [MeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X] (A : Set X) (d : ℝ≥0),
 (dimH A < (d : ℝ≥0∞) → MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure (d : ℝ) A = 0) ∧
 ((d : ℝ≥0∞) < dimH A → MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure (d : ℝ) A = ⊤) ∧
 (MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure (d : ℝ) A ≠ ⊤ → dimH A ≤ (d : ℝ≥0∞)) ∧
 (MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure (d : ℝ) A = ⊤ → (d : ℝ≥0∞) ≤ dimH A) := by
  intro X _ _ _ A d
  exact ⟨(fun h => hausdorffMeasure_of_dimH_lt (s := A) (d := d) h),
    (fun h => hausdorffMeasure_of_lt_dimH (s := A) (d := d) h),
    (fun h => dimH_le_of_hausdorffMeasure_ne_top (s := A) (d := d) h),
    (fun h => le_dimH_of_hausdorffMeasure_eq_top (s := A) (d := d) h)⟩
set_option Elab.async false in
theorem B006 : ∀ {X : Type*} [EMetricSpace X] {s t : Set X}, s ⊆ t → dimH s ≤ dimH t := by
  exact @dimH_mono
set_option Elab.async false in
theorem B007 : ∀ {X Y : Type*} [EMetricSpace X] [EMetricSpace Y] {f : X → Y},
 Isometry f → ∀ s : Set X, dimH (f '' s) = dimH s := by
  exact @Isometry.dimH_image
set_option Elab.async false in
theorem B008 : ∀ {V W : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [NormedSpace ℝ V]
 [NormedAddCommGroup W] [NormedSpace ℝ W] (e : V ≃L[ℝ] W) (S : Set V),
 dimH (e '' S) = dimH S := by
  intro V W _ _ _ _ e S
  exact ContinuousLinearEquiv.dimH_image (𝕜 := ℝ) e S

end YuiBasis
